questions.topic: Computing Devices I (Pre-computing Age to 19th Century)
questions.stem: Which early calculating aid used rows of beads slid along rods to represent numbers?
questions.explanation: The abacus represents digits by the positions of beads on rods or wires.

questions.topic: Computing Devices I (Pre-computing Age to 19th Century)
questions.stem: The punched-card idea that Herman Hollerith later used for the United States census was first applied to control which machine?
questions.explanation: Joseph Marie Jacquard used punched cards to control the patterns woven by his loom.

questions.topic: Computing Devices I (Pre-computing Age to 19th Century)
questions.stem: Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine is regarded as the forerunner of the modern computer mainly because it
options: was the first machine to be built with vacuum valves
could only add and subtract numbers
was used to count a national census
was the first machine powered by electricity
had a store and a mill, the ideas behind memory and processor

questions.topic: Computing Devices II (20th Century to Date)

questions.topic: Computing Devices II (20th Century to Date)

questions.topic: Computing Devices II (20th Century to Date)

questions.explanation: The fifth generation is associated with artificial intelligence.

questions.stem: The physical parts of a computer that can be seen and touched are called

questions.stem: In a computer system, the people who operate, programme and manage the computer are known as

printing reports of user activity only

questions.explanation: The Cybercrimes Act of 2015 (amended 2024) covers computer-related offences in Nigeria.

questions.explanation: Plotters draw precise lines on large sheets.

To recover the data if the original is lost or damaged

questions.explanation: Files deleted from a hard disk usually go to the Recycle Bin first.

questions.stem: Starting a computer that was completely switched off is called

options: To allow open files to be saved and the system to close safely
To make the monitor brighter the next day

questions.stem: Convert the binary number 101101 to decimal.

questions.stem: A specialist in Lagos uses a live video link and digital test results to advise a nurse treating a patient in a village health centre. This application of ICT is

questions.explanation: A browser retrieves and displays web pages.

questions.explanation: Machine language is binary code executed directly by the processor.

questions.stem: A language that uses mnemonics such as ADD and MOV and needs an assembler to translate it is
questions.explanation: Assembly language uses mnemonic codes translated by an assembler.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of high-level languages over machine language?
options: They are easier to learn, read and correct
They are written only in binary digits
They are tied to one particular processor

questions.explanation: A diamond shows a decision with yes/no branches.

questions.stem:
(a) State two features each of first-generation and third-generation computers. [4 marks]
(b) Name the electronic component that characterises each of the following generations: (i) second generation; (ii) fourth generation. [2 marks]
(c) Give two reasons why modern computers are smaller and more reliable than those of the first generation. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: first generation used vacuum tubes
1 mark: first generation was very large, generated much heat / used machine language
1 mark: third generation used integrated circuits
1 mark: third generation was smaller, faster, used keyboards/monitors and operating systems
1 mark: second generation: transistors
1 mark: fourth generation: microprocessor (LSI/VLSI chips)
2 marks: components are miniaturised on chips, so fewer separate parts and connections to fail
2 marks: chips use far less power and produce less heat, so there is less overheating and breakdown
questions.explanation: First generation: vacuum tubes, huge size, high heat and power use, machine language, punched cards. Third generation: integrated circuits, smaller, faster, keyboards and monitors, operating systems allowing multiprogramming. Second generation used transistors; fourth used microprocessors built with LSI/VLSI. Modern computers are small and reliable because thousands of millions of transistors sit on one chip, cutting size and the number of joints, and chips consume less power and give off little heat.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between data and information, giving one school example of each. [4 marks]
(b) List four qualities of good information. [4 marks]
(c) State two methods of collecting data. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: data are raw, unprocessed facts
1 mark: example of data, e.g. individual test scores
1 mark: information is processed data that is meaningful
1 mark: example of information, e.g. class position list or report card
1 mark: accurate
1 mark: timely
1 mark: complete
1 mark: relevant (or clear/concise/cost-effective)
1 mark: questionnaires / interviews
1 mark: observation / forms / sensors / registers
questions.explanation: Data are raw facts such as each student's mark in a test; information is the result of processing data into a meaningful form, such as a ranked result sheet. Good information is accurate, timely, complete, relevant, clear and economical to produce. Data may be collected through questionnaires, interviews, observation, forms, registers or automatic sensors.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term "security breach" as used in computing. [2 marks]
(b) State four sources of security breaches in a computer system. [4 marks]
(c) Describe four measures that a school can take to prevent security breaches on its computers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: unauthorised access to, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of data or computer resources
1 mark: viruses/malware
1 mark: hacking / unauthorised access
1 mark: weak or shared passwords
1 mark: careless or dishonest staff, phishing, unprotected network, theft of hardware
1 mark: use of strong passwords and user accounts
1 mark: installing and updating antivirus software
1 mark: use of firewalls / encryption
1 mark: physical security (locked laboratory) / regular back-ups / user training
questions.explanation: A security breach occurs when someone gains unauthorised access to a computer system or its data, or when data is altered, stolen or destroyed. Sources include malware, hackers, weak passwords, phishing, careless users, unsecured Wi-Fi and theft of equipment. A school can enforce strong passwords, install and update antivirus software, use a firewall and encryption, lock the computer laboratory, keep back-ups and train users.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three main components of the central processing unit. [3 marks]
(b) State one function of each component named in (a). [3 marks]
(c) Describe briefly the four steps of the machine (fetch-execute) cycle. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: control unit
1 mark: arithmetic and logic unit
1 mark: registers (or main memory, accepted where taught as part of CPU)
1 mark: control unit directs and coordinates all operations
1 mark: ALU performs arithmetic and logical comparisons
1 mark: registers hold data/instructions/addresses temporarily during processing
1 mark: fetch: instruction obtained from memory using the program counter
1 mark: decode: control unit interprets the instruction
1 mark: execute: the operation is carried out
1 mark: store: the result is written to a register or memory
questions.explanation: The CPU has the control unit, the arithmetic and logic unit and registers. The control unit fetches and decodes instructions and directs other units; the ALU does calculations and comparisons; registers are fast temporary stores such as the program counter and accumulator. In the machine cycle the instruction is fetched from memory, decoded, executed and its result stored before the next instruction is fetched.

questions.stem:
(a) Draw up the truth table for a two-input NOR gate with inputs A and B. [4 marks]
(b) A circuit has inputs A and B. A passes through a NOT gate, and the output of the NOT gate is combined with B in an AND gate to give output X. Construct the truth table for X. [4 marks]
(c) Write the Boolean expression for the circuit in (b). [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: A=0, B=0 gives 1
1 mark: A=0, B=1 gives 0
1 mark: A=1, B=0 gives 0
1 mark: A=1, B=1 gives 0
1 mark: A=0, B=0: X=0
1 mark: A=0, B=1: X=1
1 mark: A=1, B=0: X=0
1 mark: A=1, B=1: X=0
2 marks: X = (NOT A) AND B, i.e. X = A'.B
questions.explanation: NOR is OR followed by NOT, so it gives 1 only when both inputs are 0. For X = (NOT A) AND B, NOT A is 1 only when A = 0, so X is 1 only for A = 0, B = 1. The expression is X = A'B (A-bar AND B).

questions.stem:
(a) Define an operating system. [2 marks]
(b) Name two examples of operating systems used on personal computers and one used on mobile phones. [3 marks]
(c) Explain five functions of an operating system. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides an interface between the user and the computer
1 mark: Windows
1 mark: Linux / macOS
1 mark: Android / iOS
1 mark: process (processor) management
1 mark: memory management
1 mark: file management
1 mark: device (input/output) management
1 mark: security / user interface / error handling
questions.explanation: An operating system is the main system software that controls the hardware, manages resources and lets users and application programs use the computer. Examples are Windows, Linux and macOS on PCs and Android or iOS on phones. It schedules the processor, allocates memory, organises files and folders, controls devices through drivers, provides the user interface and protects the system with log-ins and permissions.

questions.stem:
A teacher entered the scores of five students in a spreadsheet: B2 = 56, B3 = 72, B4 = 48, B5 = 90, B6 = 64.
(a) Write a formula, using a function, to find the total of the scores and state the result. [2 marks]
(b) Write a formula to find the average score and state the result. [2 marks]
(c) Write a formula to find the highest score and state the result. [2 marks]
(d) Explain the difference between relative and absolute cell referencing, giving an example of an absolute reference. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: =SUM(B2:B6)
1 mark: 330
1 mark: =AVERAGE(B2:B6)
1 mark: 66
1 mark: =MAX(B2:B6)
1 mark: 90
1 mark: relative references change when the formula is copied to another cell
1 mark: absolute references stay fixed when copied
1 mark: absolute reference uses dollar signs
1 mark: example such as $B$2
questions.explanation: Total = 56 + 72 + 48 + 90 + 64 = 330 using =SUM(B2:B6). Average = 330 / 5 = 66 using =AVERAGE(B2:B6). Highest = 90 using =MAX(B2:B6). A relative reference (B2) adjusts when a formula is copied; an absolute reference ($B$2) is locked with dollar signs and always points to the same cell.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a computer network? [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between a LAN and a WAN. [2 marks]
(c) With the aid of a description (no drawing required), explain the bus and star topologies, giving one advantage of each. [4 marks]
(d) State two benefits of networking computers in a school. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: two or more computers/devices linked to share data, resources and communicate
1 mark: LAN covers a small area such as a building or campus
1 mark: WAN covers a large geographical area such as a country or the world
1 mark: bus: all nodes connected to a single backbone cable with terminators
1 mark: bus advantage: cheap / uses little cable
1 mark: star: each node connected to a central hub or switch
1 mark: star advantage: failure of one cable affects only one node / easy to add nodes
1 mark: sharing printers, Internet and files
1 mark: central storage/back-up, communication, easier administration
questions.explanation: A network is a set of computers and devices connected to share resources and exchange data. A LAN serves a small area; a WAN spans cities or countries. In a bus topology nodes share one backbone cable (cheap, little cabling); in a star topology each node connects to a central switch (a single cable fault affects only one node). Schools benefit by sharing printers, Internet access and files, central back-up and communication.

questions.stem:
(a) Write a BASIC program to read the length and breadth of a rectangle and print its area and perimeter. [6 marks]
(b) State the output of the program when the length is 9 and the breadth is 4. [2 marks]
(c) State the function of the REM statement in BASIC. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: line numbers and REM/title acceptable
1 mark: INPUT L, B (or READ with DATA)
1 mark: LET A = L * B
1 mark: LET P = 2 * (L + B)
1 mark: PRINT A, P
1 mark: END
1 mark: area 36
1 mark: perimeter 26
2 marks: REM inserts remarks/comments that explain the program and are not executed
questions.explanation: Example: 10 REM RECTANGLE 20 INPUT L, B 30 LET A = L * B 40 LET P = 2 * (L + B) 50 PRINT "AREA ="; A, "PERIMETER ="; P 60 END. With L = 9 and B = 4, area = 36 and perimeter = 2 x 13 = 26. REM lines are comments for documentation and are ignored when the program runs.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) A student has typed a two-page school newsletter in a word processor.
(a) Describe the steps for: (i) making the heading bold and centred; (ii) changing the line spacing of the whole document to 1.5; (iii) inserting page numbers at the bottom of each page. [9 marks]
(b) State the steps for saving the document with the name NEWSLETTER in a folder called CLUB on the desktop. [4 marks]
(c) Give two reasons why a user should preview a document before printing. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: select/highlight the heading
1 mark: click Bold (or Ctrl + B)
1 mark: click Centre alignment (or Ctrl + E)
1 mark: select the whole document (Ctrl + A)
1 mark: open Paragraph / Line and Paragraph Spacing
1 mark: choose 1.5 and confirm
1 mark: click the Insert tab
1 mark: choose Page Number
1 mark: select Bottom of Page and a style
1 mark: click File then Save As
1 mark: browse to Desktop and open/create the folder CLUB
1 mark: type NEWSLETTER in the file name box
1 mark: click Save
1 mark: to check layout and margins before using paper/ink
1 mark: to detect errors such as blank pages or wrong page breaks
questions.explanation: Heading: highlight it, click B (Ctrl + B) and the Centre button (Ctrl + E). Spacing: Ctrl + A, then Home > Paragraph > Line spacing 1.5 > OK. Page numbers: Insert > Page Number > Bottom of Page > choose a style. Saving: File > Save As > Desktop > CLUB folder (create with New Folder if needed) > type NEWSLETTER > Save. Print preview lets the user check layout, margins and page breaks, saving paper and ink.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) The table below shows sales by a school bookshop, entered in a spreadsheet starting at cell A1.
A1: Item, B1: Unit Price (N), C1: Quantity, D1: Amount (N)
A2: Exercise book, B2: 250, C2: 40
A3: Biro, B3: 150, C3: 60
A4: Ruler, B4: 300, C4: 25
A5: Mathematical set, B5: 1800, C5: 8
(a) Write the formula to be entered in D2 and state how it can be copied to D3:D5. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the values that will appear in D2, D3, D4 and D5. [4 marks]
(c) Write the formula for the total amount in D6 and state its value. [2 marks]
(d) Write a formula in E2 that displays "HIGH" if the amount in D2 is at least 10000 and "LOW" otherwise, and state which items will show HIGH. [4 marks]
(e) Name the type of chart most suitable for comparing the amounts of the four items. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: =B2*C2
2 marks: drag the fill handle from D2 down to D5 (or copy and paste)
1 mark: D2 = 10000
1 mark: D3 = 9000
1 mark: D4 = 7500
1 mark: D5 = 14400
1 mark: =SUM(D2:D5)
1 mark: 40900
2 marks: =IF(D2>=10000,"HIGH","LOW")
2 marks: Exercise book and Mathematical set
2 marks: column (bar) chart
questions.explanation: D2 = 250 x 40 = 10000; D3 = 150 x 60 = 9000; D4 = 300 x 25 = 7500; D5 = 1800 x 8 = 14400; total 40900 using =SUM(D2:D5). =IF(D2>=10000,"HIGH","LOW") gives HIGH for the exercise book (10000) and the mathematical set (14400). A column or bar chart compares separate categories best.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) A school librarian wants to create a database table named BOOKS with the fields: BookID, Title, Author, YearBought, Price.
(a) Suggest a suitable data type for each of the five fields. [5 marks]
(b) State which field should be the primary key and why. [2 marks]
(c) Describe the steps for creating the table in Design View. [4 marks]
(d) State the criteria to be typed in a query to list only books costing more than N5000, and name the field under which it is typed. [2 marks]
(e) State two advantages of keeping library records in a database rather than in an exercise book. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: BookID: Short Text or AutoNumber
1 mark: Title: Short Text
1 mark: Author: Short Text
1 mark: YearBought: Number
1 mark: Price: Currency (or Number)
1 mark: BookID
1 mark: it is unique for every book
1 mark: open the database and choose Create > Table Design
1 mark: type each field name and select its data type
1 mark: set BookID as primary key
1 mark: save the table as BOOKS
1 mark: >5000
1 mark: typed in the Criteria row under Price
1 mark: fast searching and sorting
1 mark: less duplication / easy update / reports can be produced
questions.explanation: Suitable types: BookID AutoNumber/Short Text, Title and Author Short Text, YearBought Number, Price Currency. BookID is the primary key because no two books share it. In Access: Create > Table Design, enter field names and types, right-click BookID > Primary Key, save as BOOKS. In a query, type >5000 in the Criteria row of the Price column. A database allows quick search, sorting, reports and easy updates with less duplication.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) A student is preparing a six-slide presentation on "Road Safety" for an assembly.
(a) Describe how to: (i) start a new blank presentation; (ii) insert a new slide with the Title and Content layout; (iii) apply a design theme to all slides. [6 marks]
(b) Describe how to insert a picture saved on the computer into slide 3. [3 marks]
(c) Explain how to make the bullet points on slide 4 appear one at a time. [3 marks]
(d) Give three rules for designing slides that are easy for an audience to read. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: launch the presentation program (e.g. PowerPoint)
1 mark: choose Blank Presentation
1 mark: Home > New Slide
1 mark: choose Title and Content layout
1 mark: click the Design tab
1 mark: click the chosen theme (applies to all slides)
1 mark: select slide 3 and click Insert
1 mark: Pictures > This Device
1 mark: browse, select the picture and click Insert
1 mark: select the bullet text box on slide 4
1 mark: Animations tab, choose an entrance effect
1 mark: Effect Options > By Paragraph / set On Click
1 mark: use large, clear fonts
1 mark: limit text per slide (few bullet points)
1 mark: use contrasting colours between text and background
questions.explanation: Open PowerPoint > Blank Presentation; Home > New Slide > Title and Content; Design tab > choose a theme. Insert > Pictures > This Device > choose file > Insert. For slide 4, select the bullet placeholder, Animations > e.g. Fade/Appear > Effect Options > By Paragraph, each starting On Click. Keep fonts large, text short, colours contrasting and use consistent design.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) Using Windows File Explorer:
(a) Describe the steps to create a folder named SS3_PROJECTS in the Documents folder. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how to copy a file called essay.docx from a flash drive into the SS3_PROJECTS folder. [4 marks]
(c) Describe how to rename the copied file to final_essay.docx. [3 marks]
(d) State the meaning of each of the following file extensions: (i) .xlsx (ii) .pdf (iii) .jpg (iv) .exe [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: open File Explorer
1 mark: open the Documents folder
1 mark: right-click > New > Folder (or New folder button)
1 mark: type SS3_PROJECTS and press Enter
1 mark: open the flash drive in File Explorer
1 mark: right-click essay.docx and choose Copy (Ctrl + C)
1 mark: open SS3_PROJECTS
1 mark: right-click > Paste (Ctrl + V)
1 mark: right-click the file (or press F2)
1 mark: choose Rename
1 mark: type final_essay.docx and press Enter
1 mark: .xlsx: Excel workbook (spreadsheet)
1 mark: .pdf: Portable Document Format file
1 mark: .jpg: JPEG image/picture
1 mark: .exe: executable program file
questions.explanation: Open File Explorer > Documents > New folder > type SS3_PROJECTS > Enter. Open the flash drive, right-click essay.docx > Copy, open SS3_PROJECTS, right-click > Paste. Select the file, press F2 (or right-click > Rename), type final_essay.docx, Enter. .xlsx is an Excel workbook, .pdf a Portable Document Format file, .jpg a compressed image, .exe an executable program.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) Study the BASIC program below.
10 REM GRADES
20 FOR K = 1 TO 4
30 READ N$, S
40 IF S >= 70 THEN G$ = "A" ELSE IF S >= 50 THEN G$ = "C" ELSE G$ = "F"
50 PRINT N$, S, G$
60 NEXT K
70 DATA "Bisi", 74, "Musa", 49, "Chidi", 50, "Ngozi", 69
80 END
(a) State the output of the program, line by line. [8 marks]
(b) State the purpose of lines 30 and 70 taken together. [2 marks]
(c) Modify the program so that it also prints the average of the four scores after the loop. Write only the new or changed lines. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Bisi 74 A
2 marks: Musa 49 F
2 marks: Chidi 50 C
2 marks: Ngozi 69 C
2 marks: READ takes values in order from the DATA list into N$ and S
1 mark: initialise total, e.g. 15 LET T = 0
1 mark: accumulate inside loop, e.g. 55 LET T = T + S
1 mark: compute average after loop, e.g. 65 LET AV = T / 4
1 mark: print average, e.g. 66 PRINT "AVERAGE ="; AV
1 mark: correct average value 60.5 stated or program logic correct
questions.explanation: Output: Bisi 74 A; Musa 49 F (below 50); Chidi 50 C (50 is at least 50); Ngozi 69 C. READ and DATA work together: each READ takes the next values from the DATA list. Add 15 LET T = 0, 55 LET T = T + S, 65 LET AV = T / 4, 66 PRINT "AVERAGE ="; AV. The average is (74 + 49 + 50 + 69) / 4 = 242 / 4 = 60.5.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work)
(a) Write an algorithm to read three numbers and print the largest. [6 marks]
(b) Describe, in words, the flowchart symbols you would use for: (i) reading the three numbers; (ii) comparing two of them; (iii) the start and end of the flowchart. [3 marks]
(c) Trace your algorithm for the inputs 14, 31 and 27, stating each comparison and the final output. [4 marks]
(d) State two differences between an algorithm and a flowchart. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Start
1 mark: input A, B, C
1 mark: set MAX = A
1 mark: if B > MAX then MAX = B
1 mark: if C > MAX then MAX = C
1 mark: print MAX and Stop
1 mark: parallelogram for input/output
1 mark: diamond for decision
1 mark: oval/terminal for start and stop
1 mark: MAX = 14 initially
1 mark: 31 > 14 so MAX = 31
1 mark: 27 > 31 is false so MAX stays 31
1 mark: output 31
1 mark: an algorithm is written in steps/words; a flowchart is a diagram
1 mark: a flowchart uses standard symbols and arrows to show flow; an algorithm does not
questions.explanation: Algorithm: 1 Start 2 Input A, B, C 3 MAX = A 4 If B > MAX then MAX = B 5 If C > MAX then MAX = C 6 Print MAX 7 Stop. Symbols: parallelogram for input/output, diamond for decisions, oval terminals for start/stop. Trace: MAX = 14, then 31 > 14 so MAX = 31, then 27 > 31 is false; output 31. An algorithm is a written step list, while a flowchart shows the same logic as a diagram of symbols joined by arrows.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work) A student is assigned to open and close the school computer laboratory each day.
(a) List, in order, five steps the student should follow to switch on a desktop computer connected to a UPS. [5 marks]
(b) Describe the correct procedure for shutting down the computer at the end of the day. [4 marks]
(c) State two differences between cold booting and warm booting. [2 marks]
(d) State four safety rules to observe in the computer laboratory. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: check that cables are properly connected
1 mark: switch on the mains socket
1 mark: switch on the UPS/stabiliser
1 mark: switch on the system unit
1 mark: switch on the monitor and wait for the computer to boot / log in
1 mark: save all work and close open programs
1 mark: click Start > Power > Shut down
1 mark: wait for the system unit to switch off
1 mark: switch off monitor, UPS and mains socket
1 mark: cold boot starts from power-off, warm boot restarts a running computer
1 mark: cold boot runs full POST/power-up, warm boot is done with Restart or Ctrl + Alt + Del
1 mark: no eating or drinking in the laboratory
1 mark: do not touch exposed wires / handle equipment carefully
1 mark: keep the room dust-free and ventilated (air conditioning)
1 mark: sit properly and observe correct distance from the monitor / no running
questions.explanation: Start-up: check connections, switch on wall socket, then UPS, then system unit and monitor, and wait for the log-in screen. Shutdown: save work, close programs, Start > Power > Shut down, wait for it to power off, then switch off monitor, UPS and socket. A cold boot starts from power-off; a warm boot restarts a computer already on. Safety rules: no food or drinks, no loose wires, keep the lab dust-free and cool, handle equipment gently and sit correctly.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work)
(a) Describe how a student would use a web browser and a search engine to find information on "renewable energy in Nigeria". [5 marks]
(b) Explain how to bookmark a useful web page. [2 marks]
(c) Describe how to download and save a PDF document from a website to a folder on the computer. [4 marks]
(d) State four ways of judging whether information found on a website is reliable. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: open the web browser
1 mark: type the address of a search engine (e.g. www.google.com) or use the address bar
1 mark: type the keywords "renewable energy in Nigeria"
1 mark: press Enter / click Search
1 mark: click a suitable result link to open the page
1 mark: click the star / Bookmark icon
1 mark: name the bookmark and choose a folder, then Done
1 mark: click the download link of the PDF
1 mark: choose Save / Save As when prompted
1 mark: browse to the required folder
1 mark: click Save and confirm the download is complete
1 mark: check the author or organisation behind the site
1 mark: check how recent the information is
1 mark: compare with other reliable sources
1 mark: prefer official domains such as .gov.ng / .edu and check for bias
questions.explanation: Open a browser, go to a search engine, type the keywords, press Enter and open relevant results. Bookmark with the star icon and save to a folder. Click the PDF link, choose Save As, select the folder and save. Judge reliability by the author, date, agreement with other sources, the type of domain and any obvious bias or advertising.

questions.stem:
(Knowledge of practical work)
(a) Describe the steps for sending an e-mail with an attached file to two recipients, with a copy to a third person. [7 marks]
(b) Explain the difference between "Reply" and "Forward". [2 marks]
(c) Explain the use of the "Bcc" field. [2 marks]
(d) State four rules of good e-mail etiquette. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: sign in to the e-mail account
1 mark: click Compose / New
1 mark: type the two recipients' addresses in the To field separated by commas
1 mark: type the third address in the Cc field
1 mark: type a subject
1 mark: type the message body and attach the file using the paper-clip icon
1 mark: click Send
1 mark: Reply sends a response to the sender of a message
1 mark: Forward sends a received message to a new recipient
1 mark: Bcc sends a copy to recipients
1 mark: whose addresses are hidden from other recipients
1 mark: use a clear subject line
1 mark: be brief and polite
1 mark: avoid writing in capital letters (shouting)
1 mark: check spelling and attachments before sending / do not forward chain mails
questions.explanation: Sign in, click Compose, enter two addresses in To and one in Cc, type a subject and message, attach with the paper-clip icon, then Send. Reply answers the sender; Forward passes the message on to someone else. Bcc addresses receive a copy but are hidden from other recipients. Etiquette: clear subject, polite and brief language, no all-capitals, check spelling and attachments, respect privacy.
